'''''Bryonia cretica''''', also known as '''Cretan bryony''' or '''English mandrake''', is a [[perennial]] species of ''[[Bryonia]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Benarba |first1=Bachir |last2=Belhouala |first2=Khadidja |date=2024-01-18 |title=The Genus Bryonia L. (Cucurbitaceae): A Systematic Review of Its Botany, Phytochemistry, Traditional Uses, and Biological Activities |journal=Sci |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=7 |doi=10.3390/sci6010007 |doi-access=free |issn=2413-4155}}</ref>

Its flowers bloom in the summer and usually grow between 3 and 5mm. Its fruit are toxic. They have been used in traditional medicine.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bryony / RHS |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/weeds/bryony |access-date=2024-09-14 |website=www.rhs.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref>

It is a common plant in most of [[Europe]], [[North Africa]], the [[Middle East]] and [[Turkmenistan]].

==Subspecies==
Four subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Bryonia cretica'' subsp. ''acuta'' {{small|(Desf.) Tutin}} – Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, and [[Lampedusa]]
*''Bryonia cretica'' subsp. ''cretica'' – eastern Mediterranean, from Greece to Turkey, the Levant, Egypt, and Libya
*''Bryonia cretica'' subsp. ''dioica'' {{small|(Jacq.) Tutin}} – central and southern Europe, Great Britain, and North Africa
*''Bryonia cretica'' subsp. ''marmorata'' {{small|(E.Petit) Jauzein}} – Corsica and Sardinia
